theory.title: Oraciones de relativo
theory.explanation: Las relative clauses añaden información sobre personas, cosas y lugares. Usa who para personas, which para cosas, that en muchas relativas especificativas, where para lugares y whose para posesión. Las defining relative clauses identifican de quién o de qué hablamos y no llevan comas. Las non-defining añaden información extra, van entre comas y no utilizan that. En algunos casos puedes omitir who/which/that cuando son el objeto de la relativa, pero no cuando son el sujeto.
theory.tip: Fíjate en la función de cada estructura y en el contexto antes de elegir la forma verbal.

patterns.label: Who: personas
patterns.pattern: Para personas: The woman who taught me was patient.
examples:
Para personas: The woman who taught me was patient.
→ Es alguien que siempre me escucha.

patterns.label: Which: cosas
patterns.pattern: Para cosas: The book which changed my life was a gift.
examples:
Para cosas: The book which changed my life was a gift.
→ Mi tío, que vive en el extranjero, viene cada verano.

patterns.label: That: relativas especificativas
patterns.pattern: En relativas especificativas: The friend that called lives nearby.
examples:
En relativas especificativas: The friend that called lives nearby.
→ Admiro a las personas que cumplen sus promesas.

patterns.label: Where: lugares
patterns.pattern: Para lugares: This is the town where I grew up.
examples:
Para lugares: This is the town where I grew up.
→ Ese es el vecino cuyo consejo nos ayudó.

patterns.label: Whose: posesión
patterns.pattern: Para posesión: I have a cousin whose stories are fascinating.
examples:
Para posesión: I have a cousin whose stories are fascinating.
→ Tenemos muchas cosas en común, lo que facilita las conversaciones.

patterns.label: Relativas especificativas
patterns.pattern: Identifican el sustantivo y no llevan comas: People who listen carefully make good friends.
examples:
Identifican el sustantivo y no llevan comas: People who listen carefully make good friends.
→ Es un compañero que hace que todo el mundo se sienta bienvenido.

patterns.label: Relativas explicativas
patterns.pattern: Añaden información extra entre comas: My aunt, who lives in York, is a nurse.
examples:
Añaden información extra entre comas: My aunt, who lives in York, is a nurse.
→ Esta es la escuela donde se conocieron mis padres.

patterns.label: No usar that en explicativas
patterns.pattern: En relativas explicativas usa who o which, no that.
examples:
En relativas explicativas usa who o which, no that.
→ La admiro porque anima a las personas más jóvenes.

patterns.label: Pronombre relativo de objeto
patterns.pattern: Puedes omitir el pronombre objeto: The film (that) we watched was moving.
examples:
Puedes omitir el pronombre objeto: The film (that) we watched was moving.
→ Un modelo a seguir es alguien cuyas acciones inspiran a los demás.

patterns.label: Pronombre relativo de sujeto
patterns.pattern: No omitas el pronombre sujeto: The person who helped me was kind.
examples:
No omitas el pronombre sujeto: The person who helped me was kind.
→ Seguimos unidos aunque vivamos en ciudades diferentes.

items.prompt: Who noticed Aisha's curiosity?
What subject did Mrs Carter teach?
How long had Mrs Carter worked at the school?
Where did she introduce Aisha?
What did Ben's parents run?
What quality did Ben have?
What did the friends often do after school?
What career did Aisha choose?
Where does Mrs Carter volunteer now?
What does Aisha believe can influence our choices?

content.passage: When Aisha started secondary school, she met Mrs Carter, a science teacher who noticed her curiosity. Mrs Carter, who had worked at the school for twenty years, encouraged Aisha to ask questions and try difficult projects. She introduced her to a local science club where students built simple machines. Aisha also became friends with Ben, whose parents ran a small repair shop. Ben was a patient person who enjoyed explaining how things worked. The two friends shared interests and often stayed after school to finish their experiments. Years later, Aisha became an engineer. She still remembers the teacher who believed in her and the friend who made learning enjoyable. She says that people who offer support at the right moment can influence the choices we make. Mrs Carter, who now volunteers at a museum, is proud of her former student. Ben works in the family business, which has become more successful, and the friends still get along well.

items.prompt: Describe someone who has influenced an important decision in your life.
items.modelAnswer: My older cousin is someone who has influenced me a lot. She is confident and thoughtful, and she encouraged me to apply for my current course. I admire her because she listens carefully and gives honest advice.

items.prompt: Talk about a person whose qualities you admire.
items.modelAnswer: I admire my former teacher, whose patience helped many students. He was someone who always explained difficult ideas clearly and made everyone feel included.

items.prompt: Describe a place where you spent time with an important person.
items.modelAnswer: The park where my grandfather took me for walks is still special to me. It is a quiet place which reminds me of the stories he used to tell.

items.prompt: Explain what makes a good role model.
items.modelAnswer: A good role model is someone who behaves honestly and treats others with respect. Their actions, which are often more powerful than words, encourage people to improve.

items.prompt: Talk about a friend who shares your interests.
items.modelAnswer: My friend Leo is someone who enjoys music and hiking, just like me. We have a lot in common, which makes it easy to spend time together.

items.prompt: Describe a family member who has a special skill.
items.modelAnswer: My aunt, who is very creative, can repair almost anything. She is the person whose practical skills have inspired me to learn new things.

items.prompt: Talk about a colleague or classmate who helped you.
items.modelAnswer: I worked with a classmate who was very organised. She showed me a study method which helped me prepare for exams more confidently.

items.prompt: Describe someone you get along with particularly well.
items.modelAnswer: I get along well with my brother, who has a similar sense of humour. We sometimes disagree, but we respect each other's opinions.

items.prompt: Explain how people in your community support one another.
items.modelAnswer: Our neighbours are people who often help when someone has a problem. There is a local group whose members organise food collections and community events.

items.prompt: Describe a person you would like to meet and explain why.
items.modelAnswer: I'd like to meet a writer whose books have inspired me. She is someone who describes ordinary experiences in a very moving way.

content.audioTranscript: Eva: Who helped you settle into your new school? Liam: A student called Noah, who was in my class, showed me around. Eva: What was he like? Liam: He was friendly and patient. He introduced me to a teacher whose lessons were really interesting. Eva: Is that the teacher who runs the drama club? Liam: Yes, that's her. The club meets in a room where we can practise after lessons. Eva: Do you still see Noah? Liam: Of course. He's a friend who I can always rely on. We both enjoy photography, which gives us something to talk about. Eva: It sounds as if you found a good group. Liam: I did. People who make you feel welcome can change your whole experience.
